findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give AC #5 a discriminating proving check (e.g. an allow-list grep that excludes `_review_ticket_impl`, `docs/adr/`, and `docs/experiments/**` so a non-empty result means a genuine stale advertisement).

'_review_ticket_impl' STAYS and contains the substring 'review_ticket', so the discovery grep is expected to be non-empty
findings.finding: AC #5 (hand-written docs no longer advertise removed surfaces) lists target files/lines but provides no proving command that discriminates intentionally-removed advertisements from intentionally-KEPT historical mentions (ADRs, `docs/experiments/**/*.jsonl`, and the surviving `_review_ticket_impl` engine). The Testing-section grep `grep -rn "review_ticket\|rebar review " src tests docs README.md` will legitimately match the kept engine symbol and historical record, so a non-empty result cannot be read as pass/fail for this criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC #5; Testing section (final grep)
scenarios: An executor runs the grep, sees expected hits from the engine/ADRs, and cannot tell whether a stale advertisement was missed
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC #5 a command like `grep -rn 'rebar review \|review_ticket' docs README.md | grep -v '_review_ticket_impl' | grep -v -E 'docs/(adr|experiments)/'` and require it to return no hits in the user-facing docs enumerated.
